$comment: Arm definitions for the repeatable performance matrix (.github/workflows/perf-matrix.yml, issue #1004).
SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH: the workflow derives its matrix from this file and never hardcodes an arm,
so adding or retiring one is a single edit here.
WHY THIS IS COMMITTED RATHER THAN AD HOC. Two performance conclusions in this repo were confidently
wrong: a fold memory cap believed protective was CAUSING the failures it was added to prevent, and the
test suite's coverage cost was attributed to coverage when it belonged to the v8 PROVIDER. Neither was a
bad measurement - both were sound numbers carrying an unstated assumption. A matrix that lives only in a
throwaway branch cannot be re-run against a new Node, a new vitest, or a new corpus size, so the
assumption never gets retested and hardens into folklore.
EVERY ARM MUST DIFFER FROM ITS COMPARAND IN EXACTLY ONE RESPECT. Six of ten arms in an earlier matrix
were silently inert because the code under test overrode the caller's environment, and the matrix
confidently reported 'no effect' for a lever it had never varied.
ALWAYS KEEP A CONTROL ARM - one expected to show nothing. If it shows something, the harness is
reporting noise and no other arm in the run can be trusted.
HOW MANY REPETITIONS. Measured from the first 5-rep run (2026-07-28), pooled CV ~9%:
effect ~200% (the v8 coverage tax) -> n = 1     effect ~20% -> n = 5
effect  ~10%                       -> n = 12    effect  ~5% -> n = 55
The default of 5 is right-sized for LARGE-effect questions, which is what this
matrix exists to decide. It CANNOT resolve anything under ~20%: the istanbul
overhead (8-17% depending on target) needs 8-12 reps, and a 5% effect needs 55.
Do not quote a sub-20% figure from a 5-rep run - raise the repetitions instead.
THE CONTROL ARM IS THE READ-OUT FOR THIS. pages-control is configured
identically to pages-nocov, so its apparent 'effect' IS the noise floor. On the
first run it read 1.04x, needing 80 reps to call that real - i.e. correctly
indistinguishable from zero. If the control ever shows a resolvable difference,
the harness is generating noise and no other arm in that run can be trusted.
SLICING ARMS (#1017). 28% of test-job runner time is per-job setup, so the
question 'how finely should the suite be sliced' is now worth measuring rather
than assuming. These arms establish the runtime at each slicing level, INCLUDING
no sharding at all - a configuration nobody has run recently and whose cost is
quoted from memory.
ONE LEVER PER ARM. The instrumentation arms below vary exactly one thing against
a fixed slicing baseline, so a difference attributes to one cause. Bundling PERF
with a reporter change, or coverage with a shard change, is how a matrix produces
a confident answer about a combination nobody meant to test.
A packed or unsharded run is ALSO a test-hygiene probe: tests must not affect
global state, so if regrouping changes RESULTS that is a bug to fix, not a reason
to keep them apart.

arms.label: CONTROL: dataset-pages, no coverage, repeated as a second no-op arm
NO sharding: the entire suite in one job
the whole heavy project in one job
